'''Teresa Francisca Benitez-Thompson'''<ref name="NA">{{cite web |url=https://www.nvsos.gov/SOSCandidateServices/AnonymousAccess/CEFDSearchUU/CandidateDetails.aspx?o=sWX4Y%252bdydzX1Kb0uARItwA%253d%253d |title=Candidate Profile: Teresa Benitez-Thompson |publisher=[[Nevada Secretary of State]] |location=[[Carson City, Nevada]] |access-date=March 24, 2026}}</ref> (born July 25, 1978)<ref name="PVS">{{cite web |url=http://votesmart.org/candidate/biography/121895 |title=Teresa Benitez-Thompson's Biography |publisher=[[Project Vote Smart]] |access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref> is an American politician and former social worker who is the [[United States House of Representatives|United States representative-elect]] from [[Nevada's 2nd congressional district]]. Previously, she served in the [[Nevada Assembly]] from 2010 to 2022, representing the 27th district in [[Washoe County, Nevada|Washoe County]]. A member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]], she served as majority leader of the Assembly from 2016 to 2022.<ref name="Nevada_Legislature-1">{{Cite web |title=Legislator Information: Assemblywoman Teresa Benitez-Thompson |url=https://www.leg.state.nv.us/App/Legislator/A/Assembly/80th2019/27 |access-date=November 2, 2026 |website=Nevada Legislature}}</ref>

Benitez-Thompson was crowned [[Miss Nevada]] in 2002 and placed third runner-up at [[Miss America 2003]].<ref name="Goldberg2012-1">{{cite news |first=Delen |last=Goldberg |newspaper=[[Las Vegas Sun]] |title=10 past Nevada pageant winners who have gained notoriety |url=http://www.lasvegassun.com/news/2011/jun/17/many-past-nevada-pageant-winners-have-gained-notor/ |date=January 12, 2012 |access-date=July 20, 2014}}</ref>  In February 2026, she announced her candidacy for the [[U.S. House of Representatives]] in [[Nevada's 2nd congressional district]] <ref>{{cite news |url=https://thenevadaindependent.com/article/former-dem-assembly-leader-teresa-benitez-thompson-to-run-for-congress|title=Former Dem Assembly leader Teresa Benitez-Thompson to run for Congress |newspaper=The Nevada Independent |date=March 11, 2026 |access-date=March 24, 2026}}</ref>, winning the Democratic nomination and ultimately defeating Republican David Flippo in the general election.

==Early life and education==
Benitez-Thompson was born in [[Ventura, California]], where her parents met.<ref name="Leg bio" /> Her father, originally from [[Guadalajara]], struggled with substance abuse.<ref name="Racker 5/17/2026">{{cite web|url=https://thenevadaindependent.com/article/lawmaker-social-worker-pageant-queen-is-congress-next-for-teresa-benitez-thompson|title=Lawmaker. Social worker. Pageant queen. Is Congress next for Teresa Benitez-Thompson?|first=Mini|last=Racker|date=May 17, 2026|access-date=October 30, 2026|website=[[The Nevada Independent]]}}</ref> When she was four, her mother separated from him and moved the family to [[Nevada]].<ref name="rbs" /> Benitez-Thompson was raised with the help of her maternal grandparents and grew up with two sisters.<ref name="Racker 5/17/2026" /> She graduated from [[McQueen High School]] in [[Reno, Nevada|Reno]].<ref name="Leg bio" />

She earned a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in political science from the [[University of Nevada, Reno]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |date=January 1, 2011 |title=Former beauty queen eyes education funding |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/news/politics-and-government/nevada/former-beauty-queen-eyes-education-funding/ |access-date=November 1, 2026 |website=Las Vegas Review-Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> and a [[master's degree]] in [[social work]] from the [[University of Michigan]].<ref name="Leg bio">{{cite web |title=Assemblywoman Teresa Benitez-Thompson |publisher=Nevada Legislative Counsel Bureau |url=https://www.leg.state.nv.us/App/Legislator/A/Assembly/80th2019/27 |access-date=October 13, 2026}}</ref> As an undergraduate, she began competing in [[beauty pageants]] to earn scholarships.<ref name="Racker 5/17/2026" /> She was crowned [[Miss Nevada]] in 2002 and placed third runner-up at [[Miss America 2003]].<ref name="Goldberg2012-1" />

== Career ==
After university, Benitez-Thompson worked for five years as a licensed social worker helping with adoptions for children with special needs.<ref name="Racker 5/17/2026" /> She then worked for a decade as a social worker for a [[Hospice|hospice care]] company.<ref name="rbs">{{Cite news |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2015/03/19/racetogether-nevada/25040455/ |title=For Teresa Benitez-Thompson, race is no barrier to love |website=USA Today|last=Damon|first=Anjeanette|date=March 19, 2015|access-date=November 1, 2026}}</ref> After leaving the [[Nevada Assembly]], she became chief of staff to Nevada Attorney General [[Aaron Ford (Nevada politician)|Aaron Ford]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://thenevadaindependent.com/article/former-dem-assembly-leader-teresa-benitez-thompson-to-run-for-congress |title=Former Dem Assembly leader Teresa Benitez-Thompson to run for Congress |newspaper=The Nevada Independent |date=March 11, 2026 |access-date=March 24, 2026}}</ref><ref name="Nevada_Legislature_–_Assembly_Leadership,_2017_Session-1">{{cite web |url=https://www.leg.state.nv.us/App/Legislator/A/Assembly/79th2017/27|title=Nevada Legislature – Assembly Leadership, 2017 Session |publisher=Nevada Legislature |access-date=March 24, 2026}}</ref>

==Nevada Assembly==
First elected in 2010 to represent District 27 in [[Washoe County, Nevada|Washoe County]], Benitez-Thompson served as Majority Leader of the [[Nevada Assembly]] for three terms from 2016 to 2022.<ref name="Nevada_Legislature-1" />

Benitez-Thompson served on the Assembly committees on Health and Human Services, Taxation, Ways and Means, Government Affairs, and Transportation. She chaired Government Affairs and the Ways and Means Subcommittee on Audit, and served as vice chair of Ways and Means. She also served chaired the Legislative Committee on Senior Citizens, Veterans and Adults with Special Needs, and was vice chair of the Interim Committee on Cognitive Needs of Older Persons in Nevada.<ref name="Nevada_Legislature-1" /> 

=== Elections ===
*'''2020''' Benitez-Thompson was unopposed in the 2020 Democratic primary<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nvsos.gov/SOSelectionPages/results/2020StateWidePrimary/Washoe.aspx |title=2020 Washoe Primary Election Results |publisher=Secretary of State of Nevada |location=Carson City, Nevada |access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref> and won the [[2020 Nevada Assembly election|general election]] with 18,559 votes (58.47%) against [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] candidate Barb Hawn.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nvsos.gov/SOSelectionPages/results/2020StateWideGeneral/ElectionSummary.aspx |title=2020 Statewide General Election Results |publisher=Secretary of State of Nevada |location=Carson City, Nevada |access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mendez |first=Andrew |title=Election 2020: Benitez-Thompson and Hawn vie for Assembly District 27 |url=https://www.rgj.com/story/news/2020/10/07/nevada-election-2020-ballot-candidates-assembly-district-27-benitez-thompson-hawn/3593819001/ |access-date=2026-11-01 |website=Reno Gazette Journal |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilkins |first=Terell |title=Nevada Assembly: Dickman takes District 31; Anderson, Hansen, Benitez-Thompson, Krasner win races |url=https://www.rgj.com/story/news/politics/2020/11/03/election-results-2020-nevada-state-assembly-district-races/5998640002/ |access-date=2026-11-01 |website=Reno Gazette Journal |language=en-US}}</ref>
*'''2018''' Benitez-Thompson was unopposed in both the primary and [[2018 Nevada elections|general]] elections.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nvsos.gov/SOSelectionPages/results/2018StateWideGeneral/ElectionSummary.aspx |title=2018 Statewide General Election Results |publisher=Secretary of State of Nevada |location=Carson City, Nevada |access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nvsos.gov/SOSelectionPages/results/2018StateWidePrimary/ElectionSummary.aspx |title=2018 Statewide Primary Election Results |publisher=Secretary of State of Nevada |location=Carson City, Nevada |access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref>
*'''2016''' Benitez-Thompson was unopposed in the primary.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nvsos.gov/SOSelectionPages/results/2016StateWidePrimary/ElectionSummary.aspx |title=2016 Statewide Primary Election Results |publisher=Secretary of State of Nevada |location=Carson City, Nevada |access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref>  She won the [[2016 Nevada elections|general]] election with 15,080 votes (56.56%) against Republican candidate Bonnie Weber, who later became a member of the [[Reno, Nevada|Reno]] City Council.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nvsos.gov/SOSelectionPages/results/2016StateWideGeneral/ElectionSummary.aspx |title=2016 Statewide General Election Results |publisher=Secretary of State of Nevada |location=Carson City, Nevada |access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.reno.gov/government/city-council/city-council-members/ward-4-bonnie-weber |title=Ward 4 Bonnie Weber |publisher=City of Reno |access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref>
*'''2014''' Benitez-Thompson was unopposed in the primary<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nvsos.gov/SOSelectionPages/results/2014StateWidePrimary/ElectionSummary.aspx |title=2014 Statewide Primary Election Results |publisher=Secretary of State of Nevada |location=Carson City, Nevada |access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref> and won the [[2014 Nevada elections|general]] election with 7,793 votes (53.53%) against Republican nominee Rex Crouch.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nvsos.gov/SOSelectionPages/results/2014StateWideGeneral/ElectionSummary.aspx |title=2014 Statewide General Election Results |publisher=Secretary of State of Nevada |location=Carson City, Nevada |access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref>
*'''2012''' Benitez-Thompson was unopposed in the primary and won the [[2012 Nevada elections|general]] election with 14,160 votes (57.76%) against Republican nominee Tom Taber,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nvsos.gov/soselectionpages/results/2012STatewideGeneral/ElectionSummary.aspx |title=2012 Official Statewide General Election Results November 6, 2012 |publisher=[[Secretary of State of Nevada]] |location=Carson City, Nevada |access-date=November 20, 2013}}</ref> who had previously run for the Assembly in 1990.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nvsos.gov/sos/home/showpublisheddocument?id=3151 |title=1990 Primary and General Election Results  |publisher=[[Secretary of State of Nevada]] |location=Carson City, Nevada |access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref>
*'''2010''' When Democratic Assemblywoman [[Sheila Leslie]] ran for [[Nevada Senate]] and left the Assembly seat open, Benitez-Thompson won the primary with 1,451 votes (55.92%) against Byllie Andrews.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nvsos.gov/soselectionpages/results/2010STatewidePrimary/ElectionSummary.aspx |title=2010 Official Statewide Primary Election Results |publisher=Secretary of State of Nevada |location=Carson City, Nevada |access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref> She won the [[2010 Nevada elections|general]] election with 6,951 votes (63.57%) against Republican nominee Gabe Jurado.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nvsos.gov/soselectionpages/results/2010STatewideGeneral/ElectionSummary.aspx |title=2010 Official Statewide General Election Results |publisher=Secretary of State of Nevada |location=Carson City, Nevada |access-date=January 26, 2022}}</ref>

== 2026 U.S. House of Representatives campaign ==
In February 2026, Benitez-Thompson announced her candidacy for the [[U.S. House of Representatives]] in [[Nevada's 2nd congressional district]]. The district, which includes [[Reno, Nevada|Reno]] and several rural counties, has never been represented by a Democrat and voted for [[Donald Trump]] by 14 percentage points in 2024. In June, she won the Democratic primary with 45.6% of the vote, defeating seven other candidates to become the party's nominee to succeed retiring Republican incumbent [[Mark Amodei]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crampton |first=Liz |date=June 9, 2026 |title=Teresa Benitez-Thompson wins crowded Dem primary for Nevada House seat |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/06/10/benitez-thompson-wins-nevada-house-primary-00955586 |access-date=November 1, 2026 |website=Politico |language=en}}</ref>

She ultimately defeated Republican nominee David Flippo in the general election on November 4, 2026.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Browning |first=Kellen |last2=Harmon |first2=Amy |last3=Knight |first3=Heather |last4=Hubler |first4=Shawn |last5=Cameron |first5=Chris |last6=Wagner |first6=Bayliss |last7=Cochrane |first7=Emily |last8=Hulse |first8=Carl |last9=Smith |first9=Mitch |date=2026-11-03 |title=Nevada Second Congressional District 2026: Live Election Results, Benitez-Thompson vs. Flippo |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/11/03/us/elections/results-nevada-us-house-2.html |access-date=2026-11-05 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Benitez-Thompson is married to [[KOLO-TV]] chief meteorologist, former [[KRNV-DT]] chief meteorologist and former [[KTVN]] meteorologist Jeff Thompson and has four children.<ref name="Leg bio" /><ref name="rbs" />
